rounds.text: Onemi Technology Solutions Ltd (KISSHT) presents a compelling investment case underpinned by explosive operational scaling, demonstrated by a 5-year compounded sales growth of 66% [E13] and a trailing twelve-month sales growth of 63% [E15]. This top-line momentum flows powerfully into profitability, evidenced by a 3-year compounded profit growth of 117% [E17] and a TTM profit expansion of 75% [E18]. The company translates this growth into exceptional shareholder value, generating an ROE of 24.0% [E12] and an ROA of 7.94% [E7], both vastly outperforming sector benchmarks of 4.89% [E8] and 1.88% [E7] respectively. Furthermore, operating margins have expanded dramatically to 33% against 12% three years prior [E22], while the business maintains a robust rules-based screen score of 87 out of 100 [E54]. Supported by a massive scale-up in registered users to 74.6 million [E76], a pristine relative-strength rating of 100 [E44], and guided expectations of over 40% AUM growth [E68], the current valuation of 20.8x P/E [E1] severely under-appreciates this exceptional compounding machine. Conceded: [E26], [E30], [E34].

The valuation and risk profile of Onemi Technology Solutions Ltd (KISSHT) carry severe warning signs beneath headline growth figures, specifically highlighted by a severe cash generation disconnect where operating cash flow collapsed to negative ₹ 461 Cr and free cash flow to negative ₹ 471 Cr in March 2026 [E27, E28]. This results in a deeply distorted cash conversion of -1.64x against reported profit, meaning reported earnings are entirely unsupported by actual cash realization [E26]. Compounding this financial risk, total borrowings have surged dramatically from ₹ 1,562 Cr to ₹ 2,429 Cr, pushing the debt-to-equity ratio to an elevated 1.81x where total liabilities comfortably exceed the company's net worth [E30, E32]. Inside the business, insider confidence is visibly waning as promoter holdings slipped to 23.57% following a sequential quarterly reduction, triggering an institutional money flow exit signal [E34, E37]. Operational headwinds are also emerging at the margin level, demonstrated by a quarterly operating margin contraction down to 31% in June 2026 and an inconsistent quarterly margin trend over the last two quarters [E23, E25]. Furthermore, management's own commentary points to latent industry stress in small-ticket loans and multiple-lender borrowing habits that forced the company to pause lending across roughly 450 pin codes [E82, E83]. Conceded: the business displays strong trailing top-line and bottom-line growth alongside high return ratios such as an ROE of 24.0% and an ROA of 7.94% that significantly outperform sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E12, E15, E18].

The bear’s focus on negative cash flow [E27, E28] ignores the reality of a high-growth financial services firm that has successfully bolstered its capital adequacy to 40.2% following its recent IPO [E79, E80]. This capital infusion directly supports the company’s aggressive 40% AUM growth target [E68, E88], making the current cash burn a deliberate investment in scale rather than a structural failure. While the bear highlights rising debt [E32], it fails to acknowledge that the company’s credit rating has improved to A-, which management expects will meaningfully lower funding costs over the coming quarters [E87]. Conceded: the cash conversion ratio is currently negative [E26] and promoter holdings have seen a minor sequential decline [E34, E52]. However, the bear’s alarm regarding margin contraction [E23] overlooks the broader trend of increasing annual operating margins over the last four years [E24] and the successful reduction of opex as a proportion of AUM from 19.9% to 18.0% [E74]. Finally, the decision to pause lending in specific pin codes [E83] is evidence of disciplined risk management rather than a weakness, as the company has already reopened 40% of those areas based on positive signals [E83].

The bull defends the heavy cash burn as a deliberate growth investment [E27, E28, E79, E80], but ignores that operating cash flow for March 2026 hit a stark negative Rs -461 Cr alongside a -1.64x cash conversion ratio [E26, E27]. Conceded: capital adequacy in the NBFC subsidiary rose to 40.2% following the May 2026 IPO [E79, E80], yet borrowings simultaneously surged from Rs 1,562 Cr to Rs 2,429 Cr, driving debt-to-equity to an uncomfortable 1.81x [E30, E32]. While the bull credits management's risk discipline for pausing lending in 450 pin codes [E83], it downplays the underlying industry stress where bureau data reveals households taking new lines solely to service old debt [E82]. Furthermore, pointing to four-year annual margin trends [E24] does not erase the immediate warning sign of a sequential quarterly operating margin drop of two percentage points in June 2026 [E23]. Finally, institutional money flow signals negative sentiment with domestic holdings dropping to 17.64% and total promoter stake slipping to 23.57% [E34, E36, E37].

The bear mischaracterizes the cash flow situation by ignoring that the company successfully completed an IPO in May 2026, which significantly bolstered the net worth to INR 2,245 crores and raised capital adequacy to 40.2% [E79, E80]. While the bear highlights the negative cash flow [E26, E27], this is a direct result of the aggressive growth strategy that has delivered 63% sales growth and 75% profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E15, E18]. Conceded: debt-to-equity is 1.81x and borrowings have increased [E30, E32]. However, this leverage is being deployed to capture a massive market opportunity, evidenced by the fact that the company is on track to overachieve its 40% AUM growth guidance [E68, E88]. The bear’s focus on a 2% sequential margin dip [E23] ignores the broader reality that the company has achieved a 21 percentage point increase in operating margins over the last three years [E22]. Finally, the institutional outflow [E37] is countered by the company’s strong fundamental performance, including a 24% ROE and a 22.7% ROCE [E11, E12], which explains why the stock maintains a 100 relative-strength rating against the Nifty 500 [E44].

Conceded: the company completed an IPO in May 2026 that bolstered net worth to INR 2,245 crores and raised capital adequacy to 40.2% [E79, E80]. However, pointing to aggressive growth to excuse operating cash flow of minus Rs 461 Cr and a cash conversion of minus 1.64x in March 2026 ignores a severe structural disconnect between reported profits and actual cash generation [E26, E27]. Conceded: operating margins expanded by 21 percentage points over three years [E22]. Yet this trend is losing momentum, evidenced by the sequential operating margin drop to 31% in June 2026 and an inconsistent quarterly trend [E23, E25]. Furthermore, borrowings surged to Rs 2,429 Cr, pushing the debt-to-equity ratio to 1.81x where debt exceeds net worth, creating substantial leverage risk during a period when management itself paused lending across roughly 450 pin codes due to emerging industry stress in small-ticket loans [E30, E32, E82, E83]. Finally, dismissing institutional outflow ignores the measurable negative money flow and a 1.41 percentage point quarterly drop in domestic institutional holdings [E36, E37].

The company remains firmly on track with its FY27 guidance across parameters like AUM, Gross NPA, credit cost, and profitability.
evidence.quote: On the guidance for future, we remain firmly on track for the FY27 guidance we set out on different parameters, be it AUM, Gross NPA, credit cost, and profitability including ROE and ROA.

evidence.fact: Management reiterated its guidance of a 15% reduction in credit cost.
evidence.quote: We firmly hold to our guidance which we gave last quarter, which is 15% reduction in credit cost, and we are tracking well on that.

evidence.fact: Overall growth for the next 12 months is projected to be upwards of 40%.
evidence.quote: Now simple mathematics will tell you that if we have already grown 13% in one quarter, you know, we are only going to overachieve that. So the point I was making on guidance is we remain firmly confident of over-delivering on the number that we had given last quarter of 40%.

evidence.fact: For the industry, the quality of new customers has softened even as headline delinquencies in personal loans have improved.
evidence.quote: For the industry, the quality of new customers has softened even as headline delinquencies in personal loans have improved - both are true at once.

evidence.fact: Management noted that India's long-term structural credit opportunity remains promising due to economic growth and credit underpenetration.
evidence.quote: As we look ahead to FY27, we remain optimistic about India's long-term structural credit opportunity. Many reasons for that, not only economic growth that the country will see, but also the huge degree of credit under penetration which exists, while at the same time being realistic and cautious about near-term conditions.

evidence.fact: The Loan Against Property (LAP) business has 101 branches across eight states.
evidence.quote: LAP business which we started two years back, the AUM stands at INR 617 crores across 101 branches in eight states, about 7.7% of the total AUM.

evidence.fact: The company plans to add at least 80 more branches for the LAP business by the end of the financial year.
evidence.quote: We plan to have at least 80 more branches by end of this financial year.

evidence.fact: Credit cost was 6.80% of average AUM, down from 7.02% in Q4 FY26 and 8.85% in Q1 FY26.
evidence.quote: Credit cost was 6.80% of average AUM, down from 7.02% in Q4 FY26 and 8.85% in Q1 FY26.

evidence.fact: Opex as a proportion of AUM has come down from 19.9% to 18.0%.
evidence.quote: You must have seen the operating leverage some evidence of that, 19.9% cost which was opex as a proportion of AUM has already come down to 18.0% percent.

evidence.fact: Impairment cost as a percentage of average AUM fell from 9.7% in FY25 to 8.2% in FY26.
evidence.quote: But the payoff is visible - our impairment cost as a percentage of average AUM has fallen from 9.7% in FY25 to 8.2% in FY26 and in Q4 alone, it stood at 7%.

evidence.fact: Registered users grew 33% year-on-year to 74.6 million, and total customers served reached 12.25 million.
evidence.quote: The registered users grew 33% year-on-year to 74.6 million. We have now served 12.25 million customers, an increase of 26% year-on-year.

evidence.fact: On-book AUM stood at INR 3,716 crores and off-book AUM at INR 4,284 crores, representing a 46:54 split.
evidence.quote: On-book AUM of INR 3,716 crores and off-book AUM of INR 4,284 crores, a 46:54 split, supported by more than 45 lending partners.

evidence.fact: Loan Against Property (LAP) AUM stands at nearly ₹ 518 crore across 98 branches in 8 states.
evidence.quote: LAP AUM stands at nearly ₹ 518 crore, across 98 branches in 8 states, contributing 7.3% of total AUM.

evidence.fact: Net worth grew to INR 2,245 crores, supported by retained earnings, organic profitability, and the IPO completed in May 2026.
evidence.quote: Net worth grew to INR 2,245 crores, nearly four times its level in March 2023, built on retained earnings, organic profitability, and the IPO completed in May 2026.

evidence.fact: Capital adequacy in the NBFC subsidiary rose to 40.2% from 25.3% last quarter.
evidence.quote: Capital adequacy in our NBFC subsidiary rose to 40.2% from 25.3% last quarter.

evidence.fact: Approximately ₹ 630 crore of the primary issue has already been infused as fresh equity into the NBFC subsidiary, Si Creva Capital.
evidence.quote: 75% of the primary issue, approximately ₹ 630 crore have been already infused as fresh equity into our NBFC subsidiary, which is Si Creva Capital.

evidence.fact: Bureau data for the industry shows stress building up in small ticket loans and borrowers carrying debt across multiple lenders.
evidence.quote: The bureau data for the industry now shows a clear divergence beneath a calm surface. Talking about industry, headline asset quality looks benign, yet beneath the surface, stress is building, concentrated in a few places, particularly in the small ticket loans or instances of borrowers carrying debt across several lenders at once, and households taking new lines only to service old ones.

evidence.fact: Management paused lending across approximately 450 pin codes last quarter, and has since reopened about 40% of them.
evidence.quote: Just to give you an instance, last quarter, out of caution, we paused lending across roughly 450 pin codes based on what our early warning system had flagged. We have re-examined those pin codes since. The signals have turned modestly positive, and we have reopened approximately 40% of these pin codes already.

evidence.fact: Management highlighted global factors such as higher oil prices, elevated rates, geopolitical disruptions, and currency volatility as factors weighing on India.
evidence.quote: The global environment has been one of the defining themes of the recent past - higher oil prices, elevated rates, geopolitical disruptions, currency volatility, these are all the factors weighing on India too.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next 3 quarters): The company expects a cost of borrowing reduction of a minimum of 100 basis points over the next three quarters.
evidence.quote: Krishnan has already mentioned so I don't want to reiterate it, but just the point which Krishnan said, over the next three quarter, we will see a cost of fund of minimum 100 basis point improvement if not higher.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (H2 FY26): The loan against property (LAP) business is expected to achieve breakeven around Q3 of this year.
evidence.quote: Because you can’t build a business without having the initial drag. But after having achieved breakeven. Somewhere around Q3 of this year, it will only be delivering the desired ROE for which we started the business.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (next 2 years): The company expects funding costs to ease meaningfully over the coming quarters following the A- credit rating in February 2026.
evidence.quote: With our recent A- credit rating in February 2026, we expect funding costs to ease meaningfully over the coming quarters.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY27): The company targets to grow AUM at north of 40% with disciplined asset quality and calibrated risk selection in FY27.
evidence.quote: We expect to grow at north of 40% in AUM, with disciplined asset quality and calibrated risk selection, while secured business scale-up is also expected to be strong.

evidence.fact: Management commitment (FY27): The company is targeting gross NPA below 2.25% and a year-on-year reduction in impairment costs of 10%-15% for FY27.
evidence.quote: On asset quality, we are targeting gross NPA below 2.25%, year-on-year reduction in impairment costs of 10%-15%, and continued improvement in Stage-1 mix.
